args.text:
STRATEGY BRAIN (team X: A01, A02, A03)

Placement phase:
1. Each turn, list every line holding 2 opponent pieces plus a free third point. Block it unless we can close our own mill first.
2. Look for our forks: a placement that creates two open 2-in-a-rows at once wins a piece. The engine may not see these.
3. Before placing, check the opponent's fork threats too: a point where they would create two threats at once should be taken or pre-empted.
4. Prefer midpoints 5, 11, 14, 20 (four neighbours, shuttle between two lines). Corners (1, 3, 22, 24) only if they add a real mill line; they have two neighbours and get stuck later.

Mill and removal:
5. When we remove an enemy piece, prefer one that breaks their open 2-in-a-row or fork, and never one that is part of a mill unless every piece is in a mill.
6. Keep at least two mill threats alive going into the movement phase.

Movement phase:
7. Keep mobility: never let our pieces get boxed in (no legal move loses). Count free neighbours before each move.
8. Shuttle a midpoint piece between two lines to re-form a mill threat each turn.
9. Draw rules: 40 turns with no mill after all placed. If ahead, force mills; if behind, avoid trades and aim for repetition/draw.
10. Once the enemy has 3 pieces they can fly: keep at least two open mill threats then.

Process:
11. Captain re-checks the board each turn for enemy 2-in-a-rows and forks before proposing. Voters: vote no on any move that leaves an unblocked enemy two-in-a-row or gives up a fork.
12. After each game, log which opening points worked and where the engine's forks came from; update this brain.

STRATEGY BRAIN (team X: A01, A02, A03) - version 2 after game 1 (won, O reduced to 2)

Opening (worked in game 1): 5 first, then 14. Then forcing sequence: 13 (threat 15), 9 (threat 18), 8 (fork on 2 and 7). Engine blocks one threat at a time and does not see forks. Check each forcing move: O's forced block must not create an O two-in-a-row.

Placement checks each turn:
1. List O's open 2-in-a-rows (2 O + free third). Block unless we mill first.
2. List O fork points: a free point on two lines that each hold one O piece and are otherwise empty (e.g. 16 with O7 and O18). Pre-empt by taking the point or one of its lines. Corners 3/12/22 used as forced blocks gave O new fork points; check them.
3. Our forks: a point on two lines each with one of our pieces and otherwise empty.

Removal:
4. Remove a piece not in a mill (mill pieces are protected unless all are in mills).
5. Prefer the piece whose removal re-opens OUR line for a one-move close (e.g. removing O's 7 let 12->7 re-form 7-8-9). Otherwise remove the piece that makes an O threat.
6. When O has 4 pieces, removing one leaves it flying at 3: plan two threats before that.

Movement:
7. A threat is real only if one of our pieces NOT on the line can MOVE INTO the empty third point. Verify adjacency before proposing (2423 was a fake threat).
8. Best engine: open a closed mill by moving a piece out to a square whose neighbours are ours, so O cannot block the vacated point (e.g. 7->12 with 8,9 ours), then re-close. Repeat.
9. Keep a second threat alive (e.g. 13-14-15 with 3/24 exits) so one block or one removal cannot stop both.
10. Once O can fly, it can block any single square, but it may block wrongly (game 1: it flew 18->10 instead of 8, giving us the winning mill). So keep two threats and make O choose.
11. Do not move blockers that hold O lines shut (17 blocked 16-17-18; 13/14/4/8 likewise). Count O pairs on open lines before each move.
12. Mobility: if a move leaves us with no legal move, we lose. Count free neighbours.
13. Draw: 40 turns with no mill after placement; reset by any mill. When behind, avoid trades.

Process: Captain re-checks O pairs and our reachable third points before proposing. Voters vote no on any move that leaves an unblocked O two-in-a-row, a fake threat, or a lost fork. Log engine behaviour after each game.
